meta.title: The Dancing Bees
meta.textType: a school text with five paragraph topics

paragraphs: The Dancing Bees, posted by Lily. Last week, we had a science exam at school. The exam was hard, but it was over on Friday. Afterwards, Teacher Kim gave the Explorers a project about nature. "Choose one insect, and write about it," she said. We chose the bee, because Mia saw many bees in the park. The Explorers like insects, but we did not know much about bees. Do bees really dance?

Yes, they do, and the dancing is very useful. A bee finds a flower with food inside. Then it flies back to the nest and dances in front of the other bees. The dance shows which way to fly. It also shows how far the flowers are. Bees do not have a map, but they can still tell the way. A scientist watched bees for many years and discovered this fact. Soon the other bees follow the dancer and find the same flowers.

Bees need flowers, and flowers need bees. A bee goes from flower to flower and carries something yellow on its legs. This helps the plants to make fruit and new plants. Many fruits that we eat grow because of bees. Bees also make honey in the nest. One bee makes only a very small spoon of honey in its whole life. That is why honey is special.

On Saturday, Mia took photos of the bees on the flowers in the nature park. Ranger Mark told us to stay quiet and not to touch the bees. Mia took twenty photos, and we chose six of them. The best photo shows a bee on a red flower. I wrote a short text for each photo. Leo drew a small picture of the bee dance. May showed us how to upload the photos to the blog. First, she chose a photo from the folder. Then she clicked upload, and we waited. The photos were big, so it took a few minutes.

Afterwards, we read the post again, and we found one mistake. Teacher Kim checked it, and we fixed the mistake. Our post has a title, six photos, and a short text for each photo. Finally, we clicked once more, and the post went online. Grace wrote, "In Singapore, we also have bees in our school garden." Now I look at every bee in the garden, and I think about its dance.
text.summary: Lily writes about the Explorers' bee project for the class blog. She tells about the dance of the bees, flowers and honey, the photos that Mia took, and how the class puts the post online.
